rows.available: Assuming GI(s) and MN(s), every fixed affine-linear integer system of complexity at most s satisfies the generalized Hardy–Littlewood von Mangoldt asymptotic on convex bodies, with bounded size at the ambient scale. Pairwise nonparallel linear parts give complexity at most t−2 by singleton classes.
rows.needed: The surviving old41 affine lattice systems, with m<=41 nonconstant pairwise nonparallel forms in three variables, admit the weighted asymptotic for fixed coefficients and fixed cutoff L as X tends to infinity.
rows.derivation: Use the displayed local CRT parametrization and positive convex cone. Its m−1 singleton classes give complexity at most m−2<=39. Fix the lattice modulus, coefficients and cutoff L before increasing X; apply the theorem separately to finitely many surviving residue classes. Local-density lower bounds and removal of proper powers are the distinct local calculations at9516–9528.
premises: Exact affine parametrization and pairwise nonparallel forms from9460–9496.
Positive and quantitatively controlled local density from9497–9510 and9516–9528.
GI(39) and MN(39) from the next two relationships.
rows.boundary: No uniform error rate in varying L or varying coefficients. The lower-bound constant independent of L requires the separate displayed density argument; the theorem alone does not supply it.

rows.available: For a fixed Q-rational filtered nilmanifold of dimension m and degree d, every polynomial orbit and real1-bounded Lipschitz test has Möbius correlation bounded by a constant times Q to a fixed power times (1+LipF) times log(N)^(-A), uniformly in the orbit, for each fixed A>0. Constants depend on m,d,A and are ineffective.
rows.needed: MN(39) for the fixed nilsequence complexity entering the old41 finite-complexity prime theorem.
rows.derivation: Specialize to degree39 linear nilsequences and the rational bases supplied in the source remark; split real and imaginary parts when complex tests are used. Fixed geometry/Lipschitz data remain fixed before N increases.
premises: Connected simply connected nilmanifold, lattice and fixed rational Malcev basis.
Linear orbit is a polynomial orbit of the chosen degree filtration.
rows.boundary: This is Möbius orthogonality only, not a direct von Mangoldt or Gaussian weight estimate; GT Main Theorem supplies the separate transference step.

source.statement: For each fixed k>=3 and 0<delta<=1, every complex one-bounded function on [N] with normalized U^(k+1)[N] norm at least delta correlates with a one-bounded, uniformly Lipschitz linear nilsequence from one fixed finite family of connected simply connected models of step at most k.

available.statement: For each fixed k>=3 and 0<delta<=1, every complex one-bounded function on [N] with normalized U^(k+1)[N] norm at least delta correlates with a one-bounded, uniformly Lipschitz linear nilsequence from one fixed finite family of connected simply connected models of step at most k.
available.objects: Complex one-bounded functions on [N], connected simply connected nilpotent groups, lattices and fixed smooth metrics.
available.hypotheses: k>=3 fixed and normalized interval U^(k+1) norm at least delta>0.
available.quantifiers: For every fixed k and delta, all positive N and all such f; all orbit parameters allowed.
available.parameter_range: Every fixed integer k>=3 and positive delta<=1; in particular20,39 and each fixed r-1>=3.
available.uniformity: Family, Lipschitz and correlation bounds are independent of N, f and orbit parameters.
available.constants: Finite C(k,delta), positive c(k,delta); no numerical/effective bound is claimed.
available.normalizations: Zero extension divided by interval-indicator Gowers norm; complex conjugation may be moved to the test.
available.exceptional_cases: Strict published thresholds use delta/2. Bounded N is handled by finite circle interpolation.
available.limit_order: Fix k and delta, obtain the finite family and constants, then allow N, the function and all orbit parameters to vary. The assembly proof retains all component premises.

rows.needed: GI(39): for each fixed positive threshold, the normalized U40 interval lower bound gives correlation with a uniformly Lipschitz39-step linear nilsequence from a fixed finite family.
rows.derivation: Set k=39 in the accepted assembly. Family and bounds are fixed after the threshold, before interval length, function or orbit parameters. Use threshold halving if strictness requires it. All assembly component hypotheses remain as reviewed.
premises: Accepted local assembly and its explicit component inputs, not a wholesale published GTZ inverse theorem import.
rows.boundary: No new effective constant, uniformity over k, or independent reapproval of all assembly ancestors.
